scenes.title: How the herbarium files a specimen
scenes.heading: How the herbarium files a specimen
scenes.narration: A herbarium keeps pressed leaves from different plants. The curator gives each specimen a whole number and uses the remainder after division by eight to choose its tray. Tray three holds labels with remainder three. A blurred mark on a leaf label is enough to start a search, even when the specimen number is unreadable.

scenes.title: Start on the correct shelf
scenes.heading: Start on the correct shelf
scenes.narration: Look at specimen numbers from one hundred through one hundred and forty. The first multiple of eight at or above one hundred is one hundred and four. Move three places further to one hundred and seven. The earlier number in this same tray is ninety nine, outside the shelf. Which labels come after one hundred and seven?

scenes.title: Step through one tray
scenes.heading: Step through one tray
scenes.narration: Move eight labels at a time. The tray contains one hundred and seven, one hundred and fifteen, one hundred and twenty three, one hundred and thirty one, and one hundred and thirty nine from this shelf. Adding eight leaves the remainder unchanged. Consecutive entries in a single tray differ by exactly eight.

scenes.title: Read the torn collection slip
scenes.heading: Read the torn collection slip
scenes.narration: A torn slip says the specimen number lies from three hundred and twenty through three hundred and seventy, in tray three. A small pencilled note says its tens digit is twice its units digit. Do not try every label. Begin with three hundred and twenty, a multiple of eight, then add three.

scenes.title: Strike labels that miss the note
scenes.heading: Strike labels that miss the note
scenes.narration: Check the tray labels in order: three two three, three three one, three three nine, three four seven, three five five, three six three. Only the last one fits the note. Its tens digit is six and its units digit is three. The next tray label is three seven one, already past the shelf.

scenes.title: The assistant reverses two digits
scenes.heading: The assistant reverses two digits
scenes.narration: Another leaf comes from the four hundreds and belongs in tray three. The assistant copied the last two digits in reverse order. The copy is eighteen smaller than the correct number. Trading a tens digit for a units digit changes its contribution by nine times that digit. What must be true of the last two digits?

scenes.title: Make a short list from the error
scenes.heading: Make a short list from the error
scenes.narration: Write the last two digits as tens and units. Correct minus copied equals nine times tens minus nine times units. Eighteen divided by nine is two, so the tens digit exceeds the units digit by two. The possible endings are twenty, thirty one, forty two, fifty three, sixty four, seventy five, eighty six and ninety seven.

scenes.title: Restore the missing label
scenes.heading: Restore the missing label
scenes.narration: Apply the tray test to those eight candidates. Their remainders on division by eight, in order, are four, seven, two, five, zero, three, six and one. Only four hundred and seventy five belongs in tray three. Its altered copy is four hundred and fifty seven, eighteen smaller. Both clues point to the same pressed leaf.
